title: A performance refactor of AdminPermission.projects split one combined Q filter into chained .filter(teams__members=user).filter(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS) calls, so read-only team members get admin rights on any project that also belongs to some admin team.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: In the base code, when both `admin=True` and `member=True` are passed, the Q-object union `Q(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS) | Q(teams__access=READ_ONLY_ACCESS)` ensures only projects from teams with a defined access level (ADMIN or READ_ONLY) are returned. In the PR, the `else: pass` branch (reached when both flags are True) removes this constraint entirely, so `projects_from_teams` becomes `Project.

findings.explanation: In the base code, when both `admin=True` and `member=True` are passed, the Q-object union `Q(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS) | Q(teams__access=READ_ONLY_ACCESS)` ensures only projects from teams with a defined access level (ADMIN or READ_ONLY) are returned. In the PR, the `else: pass` branch (reached when both flags are True) removes this constraint entirely, so `projects_from_teams` becomes `Project.objects.filter(teams__members=user)` with no `teams__access` filter at all. This means a user who is a member of a team with no access level set (or any future access level) would incorrectly gain access to projects. Callers `public()` and `for_user()` in `readthedocs/projects/querysets.py` (lines 57–62 and 67) and `_add_from_user_projects` in `readthedocs/builds/querysets.py` all pass `admin=True, member=True`, hitting this broken path. The policy states that only two team types exist — Admin and Read Only — and that team membership grants access only according to the team's defined access level.

evidence.content:
Base code:
            filter = Q()
            if admin:
                filter |= Q(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS)
            if member:
                filter |= Q(teams__access=READ_ONLY_ACCESS)
            projects_from_teams = Project.objects.filter(filter, teams__members=user)

Team types
~~~~~~~~~~

You can create two types of teams:

* **Admin** -- Team members have full access to administer the projects assigned to the team.
* **Read Only** -- Team members are only able to read the documentation of each project, and not able to change anything about each project.

findings.suggested_fix: Replace the `else: pass` branch with an explicit filter that accepts either access level, matching the original intent: `else: projects_from_teams = projects_from_teams.filter(Q(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS) | Q(teams__access=READ_ONLY_ACCESS))`. This preserves the invariant that only teams with a recognized access level grant project access, regardless of which combination of flags is passed.
